holidays.name: Name Your PC Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to giving your computer a personality by naming it. Whether it's 'Sir Clicks-a-Lot' or 'Brenda,' your faithful machine finally gets the identity it deserves.
holidays.origin: An unofficial tech-minded observance that has circulated in online holiday calendars, encouraging people to bond with their devices through a bit of whimsy.
holidays.funFact: Naming computers has long been a practice in IT departments, where servers are often named after planets, Greek gods, or Star Trek characters to keep them easy to tell apart.

holidays.name: Absurd Person Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace your inner weirdo, celebrate the ridiculous, and let your absurd side run free without apology. Wear mismatched socks, speak in rhymes, or do the unexpected.
holidays.origin: An unofficial celebration of silliness listed on quirky holiday calendars, inspired by the philosophy of absurdism and the simple joy of not taking life too seriously.
holidays.funFact: Absurdism was popularized by philosopher Albert Camus, who compared the human search for meaning to the myth of Sisyphus endlessly pushing a boulder uphill, and concluded we must imagine Sisyphus happy.

holidays.name: National Peanut Butter Fudge Day
holidays.description: A sweet, creamy, melt-in-your-mouth celebration of the rich confection that combines two beloved treats: peanut butter and fudge. Time to break out the saucepan and the stretchy pants.
holidays.origin: A food-industry-style and fan-driven observance placed in the lead-up to the holiday baking season, giving home cooks a reason to start their sugar-fueled festivities early.
holidays.funFact: Fudge is said to have originated in the 1880s from a 'fudged' batch of caramels, and Vassar College students helped make it popular by selling homemade batches in the 1880s.

holidays.name: Universal Children's Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to promoting the welfare and rights of children around the world, with events that encourage kids to speak up and adults to listen. It's the one day the tiny humans truly get the spotlight.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations in 1954 to encourage international togetherness and awareness among children. November 20 was chosen because it marks the date the UN adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child in 1959 and the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989.
holidays.funFact: The Convention on the Rights of the Child is the most widely ratified human rights treaty in history, with nearly every country in the world having signed on.

holidays.name: Transgender Day of Remembrance
holidays.description: A solemn day of awareness honoring the memory of transgender people lost to anti-transgender violence, while calling attention to the challenges the community still faces.
holidays.origin: Started in 1999 by transgender advocate Gwendolyn Ann Smith as a vigil to honor Rita Hester, who was killed in 1998 in Allston, Massachusetts.
holidays.funFact: What began as a small web project and local vigil has grown into an annual observance held in hundreds of cities across dozens of countries.
